title: Short loops rescue late rings: every torus that reads distance plainly
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: A torus of rings reads distance without freezing exactly when it holds a short loop along which the fastest way to every ring is a single route, the square lattice's (2, 0) and (2, 1) up to the quarter turn and the triangular lattice's vectors of length root 3, or is one of finitely many small tori. The mirror image (1, 2) is late, since rule 60 reads one way round every ring.
